blocks.content: Interfaces are pure contracts, zero implementation, zero state. But sometimes you want something in between a plain interface and a full concrete class: a base class that provides SOME real, shared implementation, while still forcing subclasses to fill in the rest. That is exactly what an abstract class is for.
1. Introduction & Why It Matters

An abstract class is a class that cannot be instantiated directly, and can mix fully implemented (concrete) methods with unimplemented (abstract) methods that subclasses are required to fill in. Unlike an interface, it can also hold real state, actual fields.

Without abstract classes, you would face an awkward choice: either duplicate the exact same checkIn() logic in every Employee subtype (since a pure interface cannot share code), or write one giant concrete Employee class with a bunch of if-else branches for every employee type. Abstract classes let the shared part live in exactly one place, while still forcing every subtype to supply its own version of the part that genuinely varies.
2. Real-Life Analogy
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884671452-366483528.png
blocks.alt: A coffee recipe template with shared boiling and serving steps, but a brewing step that varies per drink

blocks.content: Think of a coffee shop’s recipe template. Boiling the water and serving the cup are exactly the same for every drink, that part is written once and followed by everyone. But the actual brewing step is completely different for an espresso versus a filter coffee, that part is deliberately left open for each specific recipe to define.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884673116-308442345.png
blocks.alt: A company onboarding template with shared steps for everyone and role-specific training that varies

blocks.content: A company’s onboarding checklist works the same way. Getting a badge photo taken and setting up a laptop is identical for every new hire, that part is shared. But the actual training content is completely different for an engineer versus someone in sales, that part is left for each team to fill in.
3. Problem It Solves & Definition
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884674560-292054695.png
blocks.alt: A pure interface sharing no code at all, contrasted with an abstract class sharing code while still forcing overrides

blocks.content: Abstract classes solve the problem of needing both shared implementation AND a guarantee that certain methods will be provided by every subclass. A pure interface cannot share checkIn()’s logic at all, every implementer would have to rewrite it identically. An abstract class solves both needs in one type.

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.content: An abstract class is a class, declared with the abstract keyword, that cannot be instantiated directly and may contain both fully implemented (concrete) methods and unimplemented (abstract) methods that every concrete subclass must override.
4. Key Terminology

["Abstract class: a class that cannot be instantiated directly, marked with the abstract keyword.","Abstract method: a method declared with no body, that every concrete subclass must implement.","Concrete method: a fully implemented method inside an abstract class, inherited as-is unless overridden.","Template method pattern: a design pattern built directly on this idea, a shared algorithm skeleton with specific steps left abstract.","Cannot instantiate directly: the compiler refuses new AbstractClassName(), since it may have unimplemented methods."]
items: Abstract class: a class that cannot be instantiated directly, marked with the abstract keyword.
Abstract method: a method declared with no body, that every concrete subclass must implement.
Concrete method: a fully implemented method inside an abstract class, inherited as-is unless overridden.
Template method pattern: a design pattern built directly on this idea, a shared algorithm skeleton with specific steps left abstract.
Cannot instantiate directly: the compiler refuses new AbstractClassName(), since it may have unimplemented methods.

9. Behind the Scenes (Why You Cannot Instantiate It)
blocks.text: 9. Behind the Scenes (Why You Cannot Instantiate It)

blocks.content: https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884679298-886536620.png
blocks.alt: The compiler rejecting a direct Employee instance while allowing a fully implemented subclass

blocks.content: If you tried new Employee("X", "E3"), the compiler rejects it immediately, Employee still has an unimplemented calculateSalary(), so no valid, complete object could ever be built from it directly. new FullTimeEmployee(...) compiles fine, because FullTimeEmployee has supplied every abstract method Employee declared, there are no gaps left to worry about.

11. Advantages & Limitations

{"headers":["Advantages","Limitations"],"rows":[["Shared logic lives in exactly one place, unlike a pure interface which cannot share any code at all.","A class can only extend one abstract class, the same single-inheritance limit as any other class."],["Still forces subclasses to implement whatever genuinely needs to differ.","Cannot be instantiated directly, always requires at least one concrete subclass to actually use it."],["Can hold real state (fields), unlike an interface.","Overusing abstract classes for things that are really just \"capabilities\" (better modeled as interfaces) can force an unnatural hierarchy."]]}
12. Common Mistakes & Best Practices
12.1 Common Mistakes

["Reaching for an abstract class when a plain interface would do, if there is no shared state or shared implementation, an interface is usually the better, more flexible fit.","Forgetting that a subclass MUST implement every abstract method, or it becomes abstract itself and cannot be instantiated either.","Putting too much shared logic in the abstract class, forcing every subclass into a rigid structure it does not really need.","Confusing \"cannot be instantiated\" with \"cannot be used,\" an abstract class is used constantly, just always through a concrete subclass."]
items: Reaching for an abstract class when a plain interface would do, if there is no shared state or shared implementation, an interface is usually the better, more flexible fit.
Forgetting that a subclass MUST implement every abstract method, or it becomes abstract itself and cannot be instantiated either.
Putting too much shared logic in the abstract class, forcing every subclass into a rigid structure it does not really need.
Confusing "cannot be instantiated" with "cannot be used," an abstract class is used constantly, just always through a concrete subclass.

blocks.content: 12.2 Best Practices

["Reach for an abstract class specifically when subclasses share real state or real implementation, not just a method signature.","Keep abstract methods focused on the parts that genuinely and meaningfully differ between subclasses.","Document what each abstract method is expected to do, since the compiler only enforces that it exists, not that it behaves correctly.","Choose interface vs abstract class based on the actual need: pure capability contract, use an interface, shared state plus partial implementation, use an abstract class."]
items: Reach for an abstract class specifically when subclasses share real state or real implementation, not just a method signature.
Keep abstract methods focused on the parts that genuinely and meaningfully differ between subclasses.
Document what each abstract method is expected to do, since the compiler only enforces that it exists, not that it behaves correctly.
Choose interface vs abstract class based on the actual need: pure capability contract, use an interface, shared state plus partial implementation, use an abstract class.

blocks.content: 13. Key Takeaways & Cheat Sheet

["An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly, and can mix concrete (shared) methods with abstract (subclass-provided) methods.","Unlike an interface, an abstract class can hold real state (fields) and constructor logic.","Every concrete subclass must implement every abstract method it inherits, or it remains abstract too.","Use an abstract class when subclasses share real implementation or state, use an interface when you only need a pure capability contract."]
items: An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly, and can mix concrete (shared) methods with abstract (subclass-provided) methods.
Unlike an interface, an abstract class can hold real state (fields) and constructor logic.
Every concrete subclass must implement every abstract method it inherits, or it remains abstract too.
Use an abstract class when subclasses share real implementation or state, use an interface when you only need a pure capability contract.

blocks.title: Interview tip
blocks.content: If asked "when would you use an abstract class over an interface," the fastest correct answer is: when subclasses genuinely share real state or implementation, not just a method signature, since only an abstract class can hold fields and concrete method bodies that every subclass inherits directly.
